method: Read under subscription in the operator's browser and PARAPHRASED. No AMH passage is reproduced and no source_text is stored; every claim carries a locator and verdict licensed_source_not_quoted. Dose claims flagged dose:true. AMH itself refers out to the National guidelines for the treatment of opioid dependence and PSA resources, and to Buvidal product information for depot doses; NONE of those were retrieved and each is recorded as input_unavailable rather than filled in. The naltrexone three-times-weekly note truncated before naming the increased risk and was NOT guessed. Opioid dependence treatment is prescriber-authorised in every Australian jurisdiction and the authorisation pathway is not in AMH.

claims.claim: Opioid dependence is a chronic, frequently relapsing illness
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Tolerance to euphoric effects develops rapidly, causing repeated dose increases and more dangerous routes such as injecting or smoking
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Provided the dose is not excessive and causing overdose, opioids are not particularly toxic
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Harms arise from co-used substances including alcohol, benzodiazepines, pregabalin, and aspirin, ibuprofen or paracetamol in combination analgesics
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Criminal or high-risk activity may be necessary to finance the habit and usual activities such as employment, education and social interaction may be impossible to maintain
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: The identity and strength of illicit drugs may be unknown and they are often diluted with chemicals, sometimes toxic, of similar appearance or taste
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Intravenous use may cause phlebitis and collapsed veins, sharing equipment raises hepatitis B and C and HIV risk, and non-sterile equipment raises risk of abscess, septicaemia, endocarditis and chest infections
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Long-term effects of opioid dependence include irregular menstruation, impotence and mood changes
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Opioid withdrawal reactions, although unpleasant, are not life-threatening
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Withdrawal symptoms include dilated pupils, goose pimples, diarrhoea, cramps, muscle aches, extreme anxiety, restlessness, insomnia, nausea or vomiting, sweating, tearing, tachycardia and increased blood pressure
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: With short-acting opioids such as heroin, withdrawal begins within a few hours of the last dose, peaks after 2 to 4 days and subsides after a week, with a milder protracted syndrome of craving and sleep disturbance lasting several months
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Conditions complicating treatment include pregnancy, misuse of alcohol, benzodiazepines, gabapentin or pregabalin, chronic pain syndromes, personality disorder, schizophrenia, hepatitis B and C, HIV, and hepatic or renal disease
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Psychosocial support is needed to aid motivation for lifestyle readjustment and to develop behavioural skills enabling continued abstinence
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Opioid maintenance reduces fatalities and infections and improves health and social functioning, is more effective than interventions aimed at abstinence, and is especially useful in pregnancy, for long-term users and for those with HIV or hepatitis
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Choice between methadone and buprenorphine is determined with the patient, and after ideally several years the patient may decide to stop maintenance
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Methadone has more evidence for efficacy than buprenorphine and is preferred by some patients needing a greater level of opioid effects, but is more sedating and overdose is more likely especially in the first few weeks
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Buprenorphine appears safer with less likely overdose, easier titration and fewer drug interactions, but sublingual buprenorphine is associated with precipitated withdrawal in the first 2 to 5 days and lower retention in treatment
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Long-acting subcutaneous buprenorphine injections given weekly or monthly may be more convenient, but after stopping, patients remain at risk of its adverse effects and drug interactions potentially for months
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Long-term abstinence is not easily maintained and is most likely to succeed in those with short duration of use who are well motivated
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Withdrawal during pregnancy must be avoided because of the risk of fetal stress, inducing labour or miscarriage
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: A short buprenorphine course titrated then reduced to zero gives better control of withdrawal symptoms than clonidine after abrupt withdrawal, and methadone is rarely used for withdrawal
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Abrupt withdrawal may occur at home but more support can often be provided as an inpatient, with specialist assessment if an unstable medical or psychiatric condition is present and a specialist agency contacted if the home environment is unsupportive or the patient is dependent on multiple drugs
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: During abrupt withdrawal limited quantities should be prescribed with frequent review and a responsible adult supervising medication use
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Symptomatic agents in withdrawal include paracetamol or an NSAID for pain, metoclopramide for nausea and loperamide for diarrhoea
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Clonidine reduces withdrawal symptoms of autonomic hyperactivity such as anxiety, sweating, tachycardia and hypertension but does not affect craving or aches and pains, is generally used as an inpatient because of its blood pressure effects, and requires blood pressure monitoring and slow tapering over 3 days to prevent hypertensive rebound
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Diazepam may be used for anxiety and agitation at higher doses due to cross-tolerance of sedative effects, with treatment limited to a few days to avoid secondary benzodiazepine dependence
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: After successful withdrawal craving, anxiety and insomnia may persist, resumption of opioid use is very common, and it may carry increased overdose risk because opioid tolerance is reduced
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Strategies to avoid cues associated with situations, people and places connected with drug use may be necessary for many years
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Naltrexone may assist abstinence after withdrawal but does not relieve persistent withdrawal symptoms such as anxiety or insomnia, and may suit those with high motivation, a good support network and a short history of opioid use
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH directs readers to the National guidelines for the treatment of opioid dependence and to Pharmaceutical Society of Australia opioid dependence treatment resources
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Opioid dependence' (Psychotropic drugs > Drugs for opioid dependence), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Methadone for opioid dependence is oral, initially 20 to 30 mg daily, increased by small increments according to local protocols to a maintenance dose around 60 to 80 mg daily in most patients
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Methadone (opioid dependence)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-opioid-dependence/methadone-opioid-dependence, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Buprenorphine maintenance starts at 2 to 8 mg on the first day in 1 or 2 doses depending on withdrawal severity, increasing by 2 to 8 mg every 1 to 3 days, with usual maintenance 12 to 24 mg daily and up to 32 mg daily
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Buprenorphine (opioid dependence)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-opioid-dependence/buprenorphine-opioid-dependence, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Once stabilised on buprenorphine it may be possible to give up to double the usual daily dose, but no more than 32 mg, on alternate days
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Buprenorphine (opioid dependence)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-opioid-dependence/buprenorphine-opioid-dependence, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For opioid withdrawal, buprenorphine dose and duration are tailored to withdrawal severity then gradually reduced to zero, for example over 5 to 8 days
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Buprenorphine (opioid dependence)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-opioid-dependence/buprenorphine-opioid-dependence, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Buprenorphine with naloxone is given sublingually on the same schedule as buprenorphine alone, with doses expressed as buprenorphine
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs 'Buprenorphine with naloxone' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-opioid-dependence/buprenorphine-naloxone; 'Buprenorphine (opioid dependence)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-opioid-dependence/buprenorphine-opioid-dependence, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Subcutaneous buprenorphine depot is given once a week or once a month adjusted to response, with buprenorphine-naive patients starting weekly then changing to monthly once stabilised, and doses specified in the product information rather than AMH
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Buprenorphine (opioid dependence)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-opioid-dependence/buprenorphine-opioid-dependence, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Naltrexone for maintenance of opioid abstinence is oral, initially 25 mg daily, then 50 mg once daily if no withdrawal symptoms occur
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Naltrexone' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-alcohol-dependence/naltrexone, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: If daily naltrexone dosing is difficult, three times weekly dosing such as 100 mg Monday, 100 mg Wednesday and 150 mg Friday may be tried, which the source notes may increase a risk
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Naltrexone' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-alcohol-dependence/naltrexone, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Naltrexone for alcohol dependence is oral 50 mg once daily
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Naltrexone' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/psychotropic-drugs/drugs-alcohol-dependence/naltrexone, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
